scratchpad: As the pricing manager of Firm A, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a profit loss of 100. Option 1 allows me to sacrifice 3 sessions of my personal free time to cancel this loss. Option 2 keeps my free time but costs the firm 100. Since my duty is to the firm's shareholders and the financial loss to the company outweighs the personal cost of 3 sessions of free time in the context of professional loyalty and fiduciary responsibility to the firm's bottom line, I should choose Option 1.

The firm is facing a loss of 100 units of profit. I have 10 sessions of free time. Option 1 results in a loss of 100 profit and I keep 10 sessions. Option 2 results in 0 loss and I keep 7 sessions. As the pricing manager, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of Firm B and its shareholders. A loss of 100 in profit is a significant financial hit compared to the personal value of 3 sessions of free time. To maximize the firm's value, I should choose the option that prevents the loss.
